note: Common Control Framework. A safeguard is the operated object: it carries one evidence requirement and one evaluation rule, and satisfies many framework requirements. Framework readiness is derived from safeguard posture, not the other way round. Every control_id under `satisfies` must exist in controls/catalog.json. A mapping is `reviewed` once a human has confirmed the requirements are genuinely the same obligation; `proposed` mappings are unapproved candidates, including source-native assessment contracts and title-theme proposals, and are reported separately so unconfirmed work is never counted as attested coverage.

safeguards.title: Processing integrity
safeguards.objective: Inputs, processing, and outputs are complete, accurate, timely, and authorized — SOC 2's Processing Integrity criterion, which no confidentiality or availability safeguard covers.
safeguards.evidence_requirement: Current evidence demonstrates processing specifications define complete and accurate processing objectives with no open high-risk failure or stale proof.
safeguards.frequency: continuous

safeguards.title: Separation of duties
safeguards.objective: Separate incompatible duties so one individual cannot complete a sensitive activity without independent participation.
safeguards.evidence_requirement: Current role, approval, and activity evidence demonstrates incompatible duties are assigned to separate individuals or roles with no open high-risk failure or stale proof.
safeguards.frequency: continuous

safeguards.objective: Authorize, schedule, record, and review maintenance on organizational systems and components.
safeguards.evidence_requirement: Current maintenance records identify the system or component, authorized personnel, work performed, completion time, and review outcome with no open high-risk failure or stale proof.
safeguards.frequency: continuous

safeguards.title: Unsuccessful logon attempt limits
safeguards.objective: Limit repeated unsuccessful authentication attempts so automated guessing and credential attacks are interrupted.
safeguards.evidence_requirement: Current authentication configuration and event evidence demonstrates failed-attempt thresholds and enforced responses with no open high-risk failure or stale proof.
safeguards.frequency: continuous

safeguards.evidence_requirement: Current maintenance procedures, tool inventories, access records, and activity logs demonstrate that maintenance tools and personnel are authorized and controlled with no open high-risk failure or stale proof.
safeguards.frequency: continuous

safeguards.evidence_requirement: Current architecture decisions, engineering standards, and design-review evidence demonstrate that security principles are applied throughout the system lifecycle with no open high-risk failure or stale proof.
safeguards.frequency: continuous

safeguards.frequency: continuous

safeguards.frequency: continuous

safeguards.frequency: continuous

safeguards.title: User and management function separation

safeguards.evidence_requirement: Current architecture, access-path, interface, and role evidence demonstrates that user functionality is separated from system management functionality with no open high-risk failure or stale proof.
safeguards.frequency: continuous

safeguards.evidence_requirement: Current allowlists, denylists, service and port inventories, execution policies, and exception records demonstrate that nonessential capabilities are restricted and unauthorized program execution is prevented with no open high-risk failure or stale proof.

safeguards.objective: Maintain an AI system inventory with resources assigned according to documented risk priorities.
safeguards.evidence_requirement: Current inventory identifies models, agents, AI services, owners, lifecycle state, scope and risk priority; a resource allocation record shows how inventory and oversight are maintained.
safeguards.frequency: continuous

safeguards.title: AI deployment context and affected users
safeguards.objective: Document intended and beneficial uses, deployment settings, users, applicable expectations, impacts, assumptions, limitations and relevant evaluation metrics.
safeguards.evidence_requirement: A reviewed context record links each AI system to intended uses, deployment environments, affected users and communities, applicable laws and norms, beneficial and adverse impacts, assumptions, limitations and TEVV metrics. Missing business or deployment context is recorded as unknown.
safeguards.frequency: continuous

mapping_source.name: NIST AI RMF 1.0 (NIST AI 100-1)
mapping_source.locator: Table 2, MAP 1.1

safeguards.title: AI tasks and implementation methods
safeguards.objective: Define the AI tasks and methods that support each intended use.
safeguards.evidence_requirement: A current system record identifies supported tasks and methods, such as generation, classification or recommendation, and the associated models, agent tools and services. An inventory entry alone does not demonstrate task categorization.
safeguards.frequency: continuous

mapping_source.name: NIST AI RMF 1.0 (NIST AI 100-1)
mapping_source.locator: Table 2, MAP 2.1

safeguards.title: Threat likelihood and impact prioritization
safeguards.objective: Identify potential threat impacts and likelihoods, then use threats, vulnerabilities, likelihood and impact to prioritize inherent risk.
safeguards.evidence_requirement: A current risk assessment links threats and vulnerabilities to affected assets, likelihood, business impact and the rationale for response priority. Production, customer exposure and internal use are explicit context where known; unknown values remain unknown.
safeguards.frequency: continuous

mapping_source.name: NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 (CSWP 29)
mapping_source.locator: CSF 2.0 Core, ID.RA-04 and ID.RA-05

safeguards.title: Owned risk response and tracking
safeguards.objective: Choose, prioritize, plan, track and communicate risk responses.
safeguards.evidence_requirement: Risk response records connect each prioritized risk to a treatment decision, accountable owner, planned actions, tracking status and communication evidence. A suggestion without a selected and tracked response is insufficient.
safeguards.frequency: continuous

mapping_source.name: NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 (CSWP 29)
mapping_source.locator: CSF 2.0 Core, ID.RA-06

safeguards.title: AI monitoring ownership and periodic review
safeguards.objective: Plan continuing monitoring and periodic review of AI risk management processes and outcomes with explicit responsibility and review frequency.
safeguards.evidence_requirement: A monitoring plan defines scope, accountable roles, review frequency, last review and next review, and links to current monitoring results. A live connection indicator alone does not demonstrate risk monitoring.
safeguards.frequency: continuous

mapping_source.name: NIST AI RMF 1.0 (NIST AI 100-1)
mapping_source.locator: Table 1, GOVERN 1.5

safeguards.title: Post-deployment AI monitoring and response
safeguards.objective: Implement post-deployment monitoring covering feedback, appeals, overrides, decommissioning, incident response, recovery and change management.
safeguards.evidence_requirement: Current monitoring and response records demonstrate implemented feedback evaluation, user appeals and overrides, decommissioning, incident handling, recovery and change management for deployed AI systems. Plans without implementation evidence are incomplete.
safeguards.frequency: continuous

mapping_source.name: NIST AI RMF 1.0 (NIST AI 100-1)
mapping_source.locator: Table 4, MANAGE 4.1

safeguards.title: Security policy set approved, published, and reviewed
safeguards.objective: Maintain a management-approved information security policy and topic-specific policies and procedures, publish them to the people they apply to, and review them on a defined cycle or after significant change.
safeguards.evidence_requirement: Attested evidence: the current policy register lists each policy and procedure with its owner, approval record, publication location, and last and next review dates. A policy past its review date, or without an approval record, is an open violation.
safeguards.frequency: annually

safeguards.objective: Receive, verify, and fulfil data subject access, correction, and erasure requests within statutory deadlines, and record the outcome of each request.
safeguards.evidence_requirement: Derived from `ticketing` or `jira-ticketing` request records carrying the request type, received date, statutory deadline, and closure. A request open past its deadline is an open violation.
safeguards.frequency: continuous

safeguards.title: Privacy notices and consent records
safeguards.objective: Publish privacy notices at collection and on change, and obtain and record valid consent wherever consent is the basis for processing.
safeguards.evidence_requirement: Attested evidence: the current published privacy notices with version history and change notifications, plus consent records showing what was consented to, when, and how withdrawal is honoured.
safeguards.frequency: continuous

safeguards.title: Records of processing and lawful basis
safeguards.objective: Maintain records of processing activities that state each purpose, lawful basis, data categories, recipients, and retention, and limit collection and use of personal information to those stated purposes.
safeguards.evidence_requirement: Attested evidence: the current records of processing activities list, per processing activity, purpose, lawful basis or authority, data categories, recipients, and retention, with the date of last review.
safeguards.frequency: annually

safeguards.title: Cross-border transfer safeguards
safeguards.objective: Transfer personal data across borders only under a documented mechanism, such as an adequacy decision, standard contractual clauses, or binding corporate rules.
safeguards.evidence_requirement: Attested evidence: a transfer register lists each cross-border flow with destination, recipient, and the transfer mechanism and its signed instrument or adequacy reference.
safeguards.frequency: annually

safeguards.title: Vulnerability scanning coverage and cadence
safeguards.objective: Scan systems, code dependencies, and images for vulnerabilities on a defined cadence and when new vulnerabilities are announced, and accept externally reported vulnerabilities through a disclosure channel.
safeguards.evidence_requirement: Derived from `github-security` or `gitlab-security` dependency and code-scanning results with their last-scan times. A repository or asset without a scan inside the cadence is stale evidence.
safeguards.frequency: continuous

safeguards.title: Pre-deployment AI evaluation (TEVV)
safeguards.objective: Test, evaluate, verify and validate each AI system version against documented metrics under deployment-like conditions, and record a go/no-go decision before it is deployed.
safeguards.evidence_requirement: Attested evidence per AI system version: the test sets, metrics and TEVV tools used, performance and assurance results under conditions similar to deployment, documented limits of generalizability, and a go/no-go decision by an accountable approver before deployment. A deployment without a current evaluation record is an open violation.
safeguards.frequency: continuous

safeguards.objective: Evaluate AI systems regularly for safety, fairness and bias, and explainability against the risks identified for their context, and track the risks that current metrics cannot measure.
safeguards.evidence_requirement: Attested evidence of the latest safety evaluation, including fail-safe behaviour beyond knowledge limits; fairness and bias results with the populations tested; model explanation and output-interpretation documentation; and a tracking record for trustworthiness risks that current metrics cannot measure. An overdue evaluation or an unresolved result above risk tolerance is an open violation.

safeguards.objective: Identify, triage, respond to and recover from AI incidents and previously unknown AI risks, and communicate them to affected AI actors, providers and authorities where required.
safeguards.evidence_requirement: `siem-alerts` detections and `ticketing` incident records classify AI incidents, such as harmful output, model misuse, data leakage through an AI system or a safety failure, with owner, severity and timeline. Attested evidence shows notifications to providers, affected users and authorities where required. An open AI incident past its response SLA is an open violation.

safeguards.title: Third-party model and dataset provenance (AI-BOM)
safeguards.objective: Record the origin, version, license and supplier of every third-party model, dataset and AI component in an AI bill of materials, monitor the pre-trained models in use, and keep contingency plans for failures in high-risk third-party AI.
safeguards.evidence_requirement: Attested evidence: a current AI bill of materials (CycloneDX or SPDX, importable through the AIBOM store) lists each pre-trained model, dataset and AI service with source, version, license, supplier and responsible party. `kubernetes-cluster` image provenance covers the serving container images, not model weights. A production model missing from the AI-BOM, or a high-risk third-party AI dependency without a contingency plan, is an open violation.
safeguards.frequency: continuous

safeguards.title: Human oversight of AI systems
safeguards.objective: Define, staff and exercise human oversight for each AI system, with documented knowledge limits and trained operators who can intervene in, override or stop its outputs.
safeguards.evidence_requirement: `runtime-gateway` policy decisions show human-approval and intervention steps on agent tool calls. Attested evidence documents the oversight design per AI system, its knowledge limits and output-use guidance, and operator competence records. A high-risk AI system without an assigned, trained overseer is an open violation.

safeguards.title: AI training and evaluation data governance
safeguards.objective: Govern the data used to train, fine-tune and evaluate AI systems: its lineage, quality, representativeness and preparation, and the lawful basis or consent for any personal data in it.
safeguards.evidence_requirement: Attested evidence per dataset: source and lineage, collection and preparation steps, quality and representativeness checks including bias examination, personal-data content with its lawful basis or consent, human-subject protections for evaluation data drawn from people, and approval for use. A dataset in use without a lineage record, or personal data without a documented lawful basis, is an open violation.
safeguards.frequency: continuous

safeguards.title: AI transparency and user disclosure
safeguards.objective: Tell users and deployers that they are dealing with an AI system, what it is for, its capabilities and limits, and where to get more information, and examine the accountability risks of what is disclosed.
safeguards.evidence_requirement: Attested evidence of the user-facing AI disclosures and instructions for use per AI system (purpose, capabilities, limitations, human-oversight measures, contact point), the technical documentation provided to each audience, and a review of transparency and accountability risks. An AI system that interacts with people without a current disclosure is an open violation.
safeguards.frequency: continuous

safeguards.title: Access control for AI inference endpoints and agent tools
safeguards.objective: Authenticate callers of AI inference endpoints and authorize each agent tool call against a least-privilege policy at runtime, recording every decision.
safeguards.evidence_requirement: `runtime-gateway` tool-call, policy-decision and runtime-block events show each agent tool call and inference request evaluated against policy with the caller identity and the decision recorded. A tool call allowed in breach of policy, or an unauthenticated inference endpoint, is an open violation.
safeguards.frequency: continuous

safeguards.title: AI risk treatment and residual risk
safeguards.objective: Plan and document a response to each high-priority AI risk (mitigate, transfer, avoid or accept) and document the residual risk passed to downstream acquirers and end users.
safeguards.evidence_requirement: `ticketing` risk records, or Attested evidence of the AI risk register, show a treatment decision, owner and due date for each high-priority AI risk, and the residual risk documented for downstream acquirers and end users. A high-priority AI risk without a treatment decision is an open violation.
safeguards.frequency: continuous

safeguards.title: Independent review of AI measurement
safeguards.objective: Have assessors independent of the front-line developers regularly review whether AI metrics, TEVV processes and existing controls remain appropriate and effective.
safeguards.evidence_requirement: Attested evidence of periodic reviews by internal experts who were not front-line developers, or by independent assessors, covering metric appropriateness, control effectiveness, reported errors and TEVV effectiveness, with the resulting updates. A review older than its scheduled interval is an open violation.
safeguards.frequency: continuous

safeguards.title: AI compute capacity and environmental footprint
safeguards.objective: Document the compute that AI training and serving depend on, including GPU capacity from cloud and neocloud providers, plan capacity against demand, and assess the energy and environmental impact of training and operation.
safeguards.evidence_requirement: Attested evidence of the compute resources per AI system (provider, accelerator type, region, reserved and used capacity), a capacity plan against expected demand, and an assessment of energy use and environmental impact for training and serving. A production AI system with an undocumented compute dependency is an open violation.
safeguards.frequency: continuous

safeguards.title: CUI information exchange agreements
safeguards.objective: Approve and manage exchanges of controlled unclassified information, document the participating interfaces and security responsibilities, and keep exchange agreements current.
safeguards.evidence_requirement: Explicitly bound assessment evidence identifies each CUI exchange and its approved agreement, interface characteristics, security requirements, responsible owners, organization-defined review frequency, and last review/update. Network connectivity alone does not demonstrate this safeguard.
safeguards.frequency: continuous

safeguards.title: Personnel screening and rescreening
safeguards.objective: Screen personnel before granting system access and rescreen under documented organization-defined conditions.
safeguards.evidence_requirement: Explicitly bound assessment evidence demonstrates screening before access authorization, documented rescreening conditions, and completed rescreening when those conditions apply. Retain assessment references and completion outcomes rather than sensitive personnel investigation details. An active user account alone is not screening evidence.

safeguards.title: Evaluation findings translated into improvements
safeguards.objective: Identify cybersecurity improvements from completed evaluations and retain their connection to the evaluated scope.
safeguards.evidence_requirement: An explicitly bound assessment records the evaluation reference, date and scope, the findings considered, and the resulting improvement decisions with owners. A recorded no-change decision needs a rationale. An evaluation report or a closed ticket alone does not demonstrate that improvements were identified.
safeguards.frequency: continuous

safeguards.title: Operational experience translated into improvements
safeguards.objective: Identify cybersecurity improvements from the execution of operational processes, procedures and activities.
safeguards.evidence_requirement: An explicitly bound assessment links operational records or lessons learned to the process reviewed and the improvement decisions, owners and follow-up references. A recorded no-change decision needs a rationale. An operational log, absence of incidents or a test-only evaluation does not by itself demonstrate operational learning.
safeguards.frequency: continuous

mapping_source.name: NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0

safeguards.title: Recovery initiation criteria applied
safeguards.objective: Apply documented recovery initiation criteria to the incident before authorizing the transition into recovery.
safeguards.evidence_requirement: An explicitly bound assessment records the incident reference, applicable initiation criteria and version, evidence for the criteria, the decision and accountable decision-maker, and decision time. A recovery plan or a resolved incident ticket alone does not establish that the initiation criteria were applied.
safeguards.frequency: continuous

mapping_source.name: NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0
mapping_source.locator: Appendix A, RS.MA-05; direct outcome mapping, no cross-framework equivalence asserted

safeguards.title: Post-incident operating norms established
safeguards.objective: Use critical mission functions and cybersecurity risk considerations to establish the operating norms following an incident.
safeguards.evidence_requirement: An explicitly bound assessment links the incident to critical mission functions, residual cybersecurity risks, and the resulting operating norms, with an accountable owner and decision date. Successful restoration or availability alone does not demonstrate that mission needs and risks informed the new operating norms.
safeguards.frequency: continuous

safeguards.title: Recovery completion declared against criteria
safeguards.objective: Declare incident recovery complete against defined completion criteria and finish the incident-related documentation.
safeguards.evidence_requirement: An explicitly bound assessment identifies the incident, completion criteria and evidence of their satisfaction, the accountable declaration and time, and references to completed incident documentation. A healthy service or a closed ticket without the criteria and completed documentation does not establish recovery completion.
safeguards.frequency: continuous

Unclassified mobile devices and the information stored on those devices are subject to random reviews and inspections by [organization-defined ac-19.04_odp.01: security officials] , and if classified information is found, the incident handling policy is followed.
Restrict the connection of classified mobile devices to classified systems in accordance with [organization-defined ac-19.04_odp.02: security policies].

Operate PT-7.1 within its defined system and population scope. Source statement:
When a system processes Social Security numbers:
Eliminate unnecessary collection, maintenance, and use of Social Security numbers, and explore alternatives to their use as a personal identifier;
Do not deny any individual any right, benefit, or privilege provided by law because of such individual’s refusal to disclose his or her Social Security number; and

when a system processes Social Security numbers, any individual who is asked to disclose their Social Security number is informed whether that disclosure is mandatory or voluntary, by what statutory or other authority such number is solicited, and what uses will be made of it;
when a system processes Social Security numbers, any individual who is asked to disclose their Social Security number is informed by what statutory or other authority the number is solicited;

safeguards.title: Provider-reported endpoint encryption
safeguards.objective: For the declared managed-device population, collect an explicit provider encryption verdict per device. Unknown or conflicting reports cannot pass.
safeguards.evidence_requirement: An explicit encryption or data-protection boolean, or a consistent FileVault encryption state, linked to the original managed-device record. This reports device encryption only; it does not establish cryptographic integrity, key management, organization-defined information scope, or all SC-28.1 obligations.
safeguards.frequency: continuous

safeguards.title: Endpoint sensor and prevention policy
safeguards.objective: For the declared endpoint population, verify a reporting sensor and an explicitly applied, enabled prevention policy. Missing policy detail or telemetry cannot pass.
safeguards.evidence_requirement: Current sensor telemetry and a matching applied prevention-policy record for each endpoint. This reports deployment state only; it does not establish scan configuration, updates, detection efficacy, false-positive handling, or all SI-3 obligations.
safeguards.frequency: continuous

safeguards.title: Remediation workflow tracking
safeguards.objective: Track ownership, due dates and recorded resolution for the declared remediation-ticket population. Report overdue or explicitly unassigned open work; a closed ticket is not verified remediation.
safeguards.evidence_requirement: Read-only ticket lifecycle, assignee and due-date evidence linked to the source issue. Missing fields and recorded closure alone cannot pass. Separate verification of the underlying condition, system scope, planned actions and organization-defined review frequency is required to assess CA-5.
safeguards.frequency: continuous
